guiding_principle: Every post makes someone feel understood before it ever asks them to do something. The ratio should run roughly 80% connection / encouragement to 20% soft invitation.

monday.name: The Reset
monday.morning_theme: Naming Sunday-night dread / Monday overwhelm; a grounding, gentle-start message.
monday.evening_theme: Validating that the first day back was hard; permission to rest.

tuesday.name: The Grind
tuesday.morning_theme: Encouragement for the "unglamorous middle" of the week — showing up when no one's watching.
tuesday.evening_theme: A reflection prompt on where you noticed God (or peace) in a small moment today.

wednesday.name: Midweek Mercy
wednesday.morning_theme: A reframe post — turning a common midweek frustration into perspective.
wednesday.evening_theme: Community post — "What's one thing you're proud of getting through this week so far?"

thursday.name: The Honest Day
thursday.morning_theme: Confession-style post — normalizing doubt, spiritual dryness, or feeling behind.
thursday.evening_theme: Prayer request post — inviting comments with what people need prayer for.

friday.name: Exhale
friday.morning_theme: Relief/permission post — the week is almost over, it's okay to feel depleted.
friday.evening_theme: Gratitude post — naming three small good things from the week.

saturday.name: Slow Living
saturday.morning_theme: Stillness/reflection content — no urgency, just presence.
saturday.evening_theme: Bible verse post, framed conversationally rather than as a scripture lesson.

sunday.name: Restoration
sunday.morning_theme: Identity/hope post tied to a fresh start.
sunday.evening_theme: Soft app-promotion post, framed as "one small thing to carry into the week."

recurring_content_types.description: "Duet this with the verse that's carried you this year," or "Tag someone who needs to see this today."
A simple open comment thread — "What's weighing on you tonight?" — moderated with care, never left unanswered by the brand voice.
Presented as a feeling first, verse second — e.g., "For the nights it feels like too much →" followed by a verse, never verse-first.
Framed as "if this helped, there's a place I go every night to put this down" rather than feature lists or calls to download.
